syllabusTopics: Limits and continuity: limits of a function, indeterminate forms, algebraic properties of limits (without proof), basic theorems on limits of algebraic, trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic functions
Continuity of a function, types of discontinuity, graphs of discontinuous function
Derivatives: derivative of a function, derivatives of algebraic, trigonometric, inverse trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic functions by definition (simple forms)
Rules of differentiation; derivatives of parametric and implicit functions; higher order derivatives
Geometric interpretation of derivative; monotonicity of a function, interval of monotonicity, extreme values of a function, concavity, points of inflection
Anti-derivatives: integration using basic integrals, integration by substitution and by parts methods
The definite integral; the definite integral as an area under the given curve; area between two curves

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Discontinuity graphs speak the decision tree's language: holes and detached dots for the removable pair, branch-end gaps for jumps, arrowed vertical walls for infinities, dense folding for oscillation. Dots record assignments, branch endpoints record approaches — reading them separately is the whole skill.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - Hole at (a, L): lim = L, f(a) undefined ⟹ open dot at (a, L) - Jump at a: branch ends at (a, LHL) and (a, RHL), LHL ≠ RHL

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Checking only that $f(a)$ is defined and declaring continuity — the limit must exist and match.  ·  Conflating continuity with differentiability — $|x|$ at 0 is continuous but not differentiable.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Where a formula is quoted it is valid only under the conditions stated; Checking only that $f(a)$ is defined and declaring continuity — the limit must exist and match.  ·  Every result here follows from the definitions, so a first-principles derivation is always a valid fallback in the exam.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***The misleading meeting*** - branches can meet at x = a while the dot sits elsewhere: the approaches agree, the assignment does not - removable, not continuous.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Using a one-sided limit in place of the two-sided one at a join point.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Work through the authored practice problems and re-derive each key formula from the definition.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Skeleton first, suspects last; arrows on every wall; dots on every seam.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB-style (5m): Describe the graph of f(x) = (x² − 4)/(x − 2) near x = 2, including the feature's type and coordinates.** — **Simplify:** f(x) = x + 2 for x ≠ 2 ⟹ the graph is the **line y = x + 2 with a hole at (2, 4)**.…  ·  **NEB-style (6m): Describe the graph of f(x) = 1/(x − 3)² near x = 3, and contrast with 1/(x − 3).** — **For 1/(x−3)²:** the denominator is a square ⟹ positive from **both** sides ⟹ both branches rise along the vertical line x = 3 toward **+∞** — a **unifying wall** (arrows both up).…

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: In sketch questions, label the coordinates of holes, dots and walls - unlabelled features earn half marks.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Every graph feature maps to one line of the classification tree; the graph is evidence, not decoration.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Visual vocabulary: hole = open dot on meeting branches (removable, value missing); detached dot = open dot + filled dot at different heights (removable, mismatch); jump = branch ends at different heights, dot on the owning side; wall = hugging vertical line with side arrows (odd splits, even unifies); oscillatory =…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Zooming into any neighbourhood of any discontinuity shows exactly one of the standard types.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: **NEB-style (6m): For f(x) = x + 1 for x < 1, f(x) = 5 − x for x ≥ 1: sketch-reason the seam at x = 1 and give the continuity verdict.** — **Left branch:** y = x + 1 on (−∞, 1), approaching height **2** at x = 1⁻ (open end — the branch's condition excludes 1).…  ·  **NEB-style (5m): A graph shows a curve with an open dot at (1, 3), a filled dot at (1, 5), and continuous branches meeting at the open dot. Classify and give the repair.** — **Reading the features:** branches meeting at height 3 ⟹ LHL = RHL = **3** (limit exists); filled dot at (1, 5) ⟹ f(1) = 5.…

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Companion Doorway to Discontinuity Graphs This canonical is the **short-form doorway** to graphs of discontinuous functions: how each break type looks on paper and how to read a graph back into a classification.…  ·  ## 2. Theorem Mirror — The Visual Vocabulary - **Hole (removable, value missing):** open dot on an otherwise continuous curve — the branches meet where the point should be. - **Detached dot (removable, mismatch):** open dot at the limit's height plus a filled dot elsewhere at x = a — the value was assigned away from the approach.…  ·  ## 3. Deep Conceptual — Reading Graphs as Evidence, Not Decoration - A graph is a **witness**: every classification claim should be checkable against it. The hole says "limit exists, value missing"; the detached dot says "limit exists, value moved"; the gap says "sides disagree"; the wall says "a side is unbounded." Each visual feature maps to exactly one line of the decision…

rows.text: NEB-style practice beyond the verified PYQs recorded on the parent canonical.  ·  Walls are unfinished without their side arrows.  ·  Sketch-reason f(x) = (x² − 4)/(x − 2) and mark the feature at x = 2.

Deep Conceptual — Sketching Strategy: Skeleton First, Suspects Last - **Draw the continuous skeleton first** (the formula's curve on its domain intervals), then decorate the suspects: holes, dots, gaps, walls. This ordering prevents the classic error of drawing the exception and forgetting the rule.…

rows.text: ## 5. Worked Example Types - **Type A — sketch from formula:** rational function ⟹ skeleton + holes at cancelled roots + walls at surviving roots with side arrows. - **Type B — read from graph:** given the picture, name each feature's type and the side continuity of each dot.…  ·  ## 6.
